text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Queen Noor urges concentrating on issues of sustained development and human rights; Prime Minister Abdul Salam al-Majali stresses the commitment of Jordan to comprehensive Middle East peace.
- Majali says "no ice on the Amman-Damascus highway" and says Jordan will follow the Arab consensus on convening or delaying the Doha economic summit.
- Amman Financial Market (AFM) maintains its upward movement; six percent increase in prices and 94 million dinars ($133 million) of trading since the start of the year.
- Trial of Jordanian soldier who shot the Israeli schoolgirls resumes on Monday; ninety-two lawyers volunteer to defend him in an expanded defence counsel.
- Government is studying proposals to encourage early retirement as part of civil service reform.
- Islamic Action Front (IAF) meet on Monday to debate their stance on the new press law.
- Fifteen million dinars ($21 million) of foreign investments enter the market during May.
- Princess Aisha visits Israeli army sites; to meet top military officials.
